text: athena land --pr judges the checks of the job's own commit, not the pull request's current head. When a fix is pushed to the pull request (on 2026-10-18, PR #149 for job 20261018-145008-k7fq), land keeps re-running and reporting the old commit's failure even though the new head is green, so the only way to merge was around land. Make land judge the checks of the pull request's current head and guard the merge with that head, and never force-replace a newer head with the job's older commit. Until the records-history build (D111) lands, a squash of a job's landing plus any later commit is not a valid landing (that is how squash 02837e0 broke the history check), so land refuses when the pull request's current head is anything other than the job's landing commit, declared intervention or not, naming each extra commit and why. This repeats job 20261019-013306-zvmr, abandoned when the machine ran out of disk mid-run.
